mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stop falling and stabilize near their current levels, weekday downtown footfall stabilizes first and then lifts RETAIL_REC over the following month because commuting and incidental shopping normalize together.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain near current levels for four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not rise above the prior 28-day mean, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A recent rise in GROCERY_PHARM above its current elevated band diverts households into essential-trip consolidation, which crowds out discretionary retail visits and pushes RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM increases by at least 2 points week-on-week from its current level
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 2 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC is not lower than its current 4-week mean within two weeks, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rebound in PARKS and RESIDENTIAL activity signals more local leisure time and neighborhood-based routines, which substitutes for mall and shopping-district visits and keeps RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both rise for four weeks yet RETAIL_REC increases relative to the last 28 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT drops sharply below its already weak level, access friction rises for shopping trips and retail visits fall within one week, because discretionary trips are more sensitive to transport disruptions than grocery trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -15 and stays there for one weekly mean
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls below -15 for a week and RETAIL_REC does not decline within the following week, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES recover while RESIDENTIAL falls back toward baseline, more people spend daytime hours outside home and convert commuting into discretionary shopping, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises while RESIDENTIAL declines by at least 1 point from its current weekly mean
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL declines by at least 1 point but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 28-day mean over the next month, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained positive PARKS signal indicates favorable outdoor conditions and leisure demand, which spills over into nearby retail spending and raises RETAIL_REC after a two-week lag.
failure_condition: If PARKS stays elevated for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve by the third week, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Under a mobility-restriction regime, a combined weakness in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES suppresses shared commuting and in-person shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC remains lower over the next month even if grocery activity stays high.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain below -10 for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both stay below -10 for two weeks and RETAIL_REC still rises relative to the prior 28 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising while RETAIL_REC stays flat, the pattern indicates spending is being absorbed by routine essential trips rather than discretionary outings, so retail-and-recreation mobility will edge down over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 29 while RETAIL_REC remains between -14 and -12
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises above 29 while RETAIL_REC stays near its current band and then RETAIL_REC increases over the next month, reject the hypothesis.
